faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Slit-Valve Protection Shunt suitable for Slit-valve plasma deposition protection shunt?
faq.a: Titanium Slit-Valve Protection Shunt uses Grade 2 CP-Ti because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address chamber shield operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Slit-Valve Protection Shunt?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Slit-Valve Protection Shunt is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for slitvalve plasma deposition requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Slit-Valve Protection Shunt require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. slitvalve plasma deposition components require Electropolishing Ra <0.25um + UHP DI cascade rinse with particle count verification per MIL-STD-1246 Class 1 — tailored for slitvalve plasma deposition application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium Slit-Valve Protection Shunt shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment of Titanium Slit-Valve Protection Shunt includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance confirming all processes meet slitvalve plasma deposition specifications; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements on critical features; (4) Surface roughness certification per applicable standards. FAIR available on request.
